title: Excessive Cabin Altitude
abstract: Emergency procedure for excessive cabin altitude, covering the oxygen and descent actions and the subsequent management of cabin pressure on manual control of the outflow valve.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the crew procedure for an excessive cabin altitude, including the immediate actions and the management of the cabin on manual control for the remainder of the flight.
sections.description: Excessive cabin altitude is announced by the warning and by the cabin altitude indication on the system page. The immediate actions are the crew oxygen masks, the emergency descent and the passenger oxygen, in that order and without reference to the cause. Only once the aircraft is at a safe altitude does the cause matter. Where the cause is a failed outflow valve control channel rather than a structural leak, the cabin can be re-established on manual control and the flight continued to a suitable airfield with the cabin managed by the crew. On the duplex actuator standard a single channel failure does not remove automatic control at all, and the crew will see a caution rather than a loss of control. Manual control behaves differently between the two fleets. On the twin-engine aircraft at the duplex standard the drive is regeared and the valve is proportional, so a small correction is possible and full travel takes about twenty seconds. On the four-engine aircraft the original two-position drive is still fitted: the valve moves slowly, full travel takes about fifty seconds, and the indicated position follows the controller rather than the valve, so the indication may not agree with what the valve is doing. Anticipate accordingly.
sections.crew_procedure: CREW OXYGEN MASKS: ON, 100 per cent. CREW COMMUNICATION: ESTABLISH. EMERGENCY DESCENT: INITIATE. PASSENGER OXYGEN: CHECK DEPLOYED. Descend to the lower of ten thousand feet and the minimum safe altitude. When level and stable, assess the cause. If the cabin can be re-established, select MAN on the overhead panel and command the valve closed, watching cabin vertical speed. On the four-engine aircraft make the input in short bursts and wait for the cabin rate to settle before the next one; the drive will otherwise overshoot. Plan the arrival so that the cabin is settled at the landing elevation before the approach. Do not return to automatic control in flight.
sections.limitation_note: Manual control of the outflow valve is permitted for the remainder of the flight following an excessive cabin altitude event. The maximum differential pressure limit is unchanged and remains the crew's responsibility to observe on manual control.
